builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TEMPO: Regime-Aware Operator Learning with Locally Adapted POD Bases
summary: TEMPO replaces a single global POD basis in PDE operator learning with a mixture of locally adapted bases discovered via EM, plus a gating network that routes inputs to per-regime branch networks. The cost is a two-phase training pipeline, added model complexity from gating and per-regime branches, and sensitivity to the EM regime discovery and routing quality. It can fail when the latent regimes are ill-separated, when the gating network misroutes inputs at inference, or when the parameter regimes in deployment data drift from those recovered offline.
rationale: This is a surrogate-modeling method for parametric PDE simulation, not a technique for training, serving, or operating LLM/ML production systems, so it falls outside the reader's production practice despite being runnable on a single GPU.
technique: Regime-aware operator learning with mixture of POD bases

claims.statement: TEMPO replaces a single global POD basis in PDE operator learning with a mixture of locally adapted bases discovered via EM, plus a gating network that routes inputs to per-regime branch networks. The cost is a two-phase training pipeline, added model complexity from gating and per-regime branches, and sensitivity to the EM regime discovery and routing quality. It can fail when the latent regimes are ill-separated, when the gating network misroutes inputs at inference, or when the parameter regimes in deployment data drift from those recovered offline.

With 64 total POD modes, TEMPO achieves 18.61% test error on Burgers' equation versus 19.61% for a global POD baseline (approximately 1 percentage point improvement), with lower errors also reported on Coanda and Helmholtz benchmarks.
